title: Crypto fraud complaints - which agency actually has jurisdiction
p1: Lost money in a crypto scam? The first question many people ask is: "Where do I complain?" The surprising part is that sending a complaint to the wrong place can delay action.
p2: Many believe every crypto fraud case goes directly to a cyber police station or a financial regulator. But jurisdiction depends on what happened. A crypto investment scam, online cheating, identity theft, or money laundering concern may involve different authorities with different roles.
p3: For most victims in India, reporting online fraud quickly through the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal and informing the cyber police can help start the process. Regulators like SEBI or RBI may become relevant in cases involving regulated entities or financial activities. The key insight: the nature of the fraud decides the agency, not just the fact that crypto was involved. Save evidence like wallet addresses, transaction details, chats, and payment records.
conclusion: Have you ever wondered why crypto fraud complaints often get redirected between agencies? What should victims do first to avoid delays?
